chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Mis'mam ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed the Farewell Stop (Ifafah) from Arafat before the sunset of the sun, he said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him, and if he was deliberate, then upon him is the sacrifice of a camel (Badanah).'
So when you intend to perform the Farewell Stop, supplicate with this supplication which he narrated:

key_terms.جَاهِل: Ignorant (one who acted out of lack of knowledge)
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat (the sacred plain where the pillar of Hajj stands)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for leaving Arafat before sunset during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for early departure from Arafat, distinguishing between ignorance (*jahil*) and deliberate action (*muta'ammid*) to determine the expiation of a *Badanah*. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) in ritual validity and concludes by linking the legal ruling to the recommended supplication for the moment of *Ifafah*, highlighting the spiritual dimension of the Hajj rites.
